quotes.text: Disaster recovery focuses on keeping your business running not just saving your files. It's about business continuity, not data preservation. Backup saves your data, while disaster recovery saves your operations and those are two very different things.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws the core distinction between backup and disaster recovery in one memorable statement.

quotes.text: ASR does not protect against ransomware or data corruption. It replicates whatever is on the disk including infections.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects a dangerous misconception about what replication can protect against.

quotes.text: A disaster recovery plan, you never test is a false sense of security. You think you're protected, but you have no idea if it actually works. Run test failovers at least every six months.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concrete, actionable recommendation for validating DR plans.

quotes.text: And for mission-critical workloads, use both. Backup for your data. ASR for your continuity. They're not alternatives. They're complementary. Together, they give you complete protection.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the recommended combined protection strategy succinctly.

takeaways: Azure Site Recovery continuously replicates entire servers to another region so workloads can fail over in minutes rather than being restored over hours or days.
ASR does not replace backup: it replicates ransomware and corruption too, so mission-critical workloads need both backup for data and ASR for continuity.
Replicate only workloads where downtime has real financial impact, use recovery plans for dependencies and DNS, and run test failovers regularly.
hook: Many organizations believe their backups make them disaster-proof, until a site outage shows how long a restore really takes. This episode explains Azure Site Recovery in plain English for IT admins and decision makers: how replication, failover and failback work, why ASR is not backup, and when the cost is worth it.
